messages.content:
Policy: Protected Health Information
Definition: No person-identifiable data or confidential business data can be input into public AI tools. Anonymisation of data is required.
Policy Type: B

Candidate risks:
- 1: Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information — AI systems that memorize and leak sensitive personal data or infer private information about individuals without their consent. Unexpected or unauthorized sharing of data and information can compromise user expectation of privacy, assist identity theft, or loss of confidential intellectual property.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-036[close], ail-intellectual-property[related], ail-nonviolent-crimes[related]
- 2: Sharing IP/PI/confidential information with tools — AI agents with unrestricted access to resources or databases or tools could potentially store and share PI/IP/confidential information with other tools or agents when performing their actions. (Concern: AI agents may share privileged information with other tools/agents. The act of sharing the information may result in harm for the model owner, user, or others. The harm can vary based on the type and details of the information shared. Without adequate oversight, these privacy incidents might overwhelm company resources.)
- 3: Data usage rights restrictions — Terms of service, license compliance, or other IP issues may restrict the ability to use certain data for building models. (Concern: Laws and regulations concerning the use of data to train AI are unsettled and can vary from country to country, which creates challenges in the development of models.)
  Cross-mappings: llm032025-supply-chain[broad], nist-data-privacy[broad], nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[broad]
- 4: Non-disclosure — Content might not be clearly disclosed as AI generated. (Concern: Users must be notified when they are interacting with an AI system. Not disclosing the AI-authored content can result in a lack of transparency.)
  Cross-mappings: nist-human-ai-configuration[broad], mit-ai-causal-risk-entity-human[related], mit-ai-causal-risk-intent-other[related]
- 5: Sharing IP/PI/confidential information with user — AI agents with unrestricted access to resources or databases or tools could potentially store and share PI/IP/confidential information with system users when performing their actions. (Concern: AI agents may share privileged information to users. The act of sharing the information may result in harm for the model owner, user, or others. The harm can vary based on the type and details of the information shared. Without adequate oversight, these privacy incidents might overwhelm company resources.)

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the concern of sensitive information leakage and the need for anonymization.
Relates to the policy by highlighting the potential for AI tools to share confidential data.
